findings.message: `normalize` removes digits from each token, then joins every token with a space, including tokens that are now empty. A digit-only token in the middle leaves a double space, so `normalize('line 42 failed')` returns `'line  failed'`, not `'line failed'`. The ticket says normalize collapses whitespace to single spaces. Because the signature hashes this string, `'a 42 b'` and `'a b'` get different signatures, and dedup misses two messages that differ only by a line number. The test misses this because both of its reasons put the number in the same place.
findings.paved_road: Remove the `/` tokens, remove the digit runs, then collapse whitespace: `' '.join(re.sub(r'\d+', '', ' '.join(t for t in reason.split() if '/' not in t)).split())`. Add a test that `normalize('a 42 b') == normalize('a b') == 'a b'`.
